An Unforgettable 24-Day Safari & Culture Journey Through India – With Raj and Wanderlust Travel Hub

From the moment we first connected with Raj from Wanderlust Travel Hub, we knew we were in the best hands. A dear mutual friend referred us to him, and after more than a year of thoughtful planning and communication, our dream of exploring India came to life in the most personal, heartfelt, and beautifully organized way imaginable.

This was our very first visit to India — a place we had always dreamed of — and what Raj created for us will stay in our hearts forever. From the start on November 7th in Delhi, we began our journey to Jim Corbett National Park, where luck was on our side — a magnificent tiger appeared beside the road just minutes before reaching our lodge! Over the next 24 days, we traveled through some of India’s most iconic national parks and cultural treasures, each day full of wonder:

- Jim Corbett and the rare Great Hornbill sightings
- The Taj Mahal and city of Agra with our a knowledgeable local guide
- Keoladeo National Park with its spectacular birdlife
- Ranthambore with its stunning fort and amazing wildlife
- Chambal Gharial Sanctuary — spotting the critically endangered gharial crocodiles
- Jaipur’s charm, history, shopping and great local streetfood
- Visits to Tadoba, Pench, Kanha, and Bandhavgarh — we had 20 safaris in total on our tour, spotting tigers, wild dogs, sloth bears, countless birds, and the endless beauty of India’s wilderness
- Our final days brought us to Khajuraho’s mesmerizing temples and the tastiest aloo chaat street food we’ve ever had! A spontaneous stop Gwalior to see the awe-inspiring Gopachal Jain Statues and Gwalior Fort was the perfect way to close this magical journey before returning to Delhi.

None of this would have been the same without Raj. Beyond being a phenomenal tour organizer, he became a true friend — someone whose warmth, humor, and genuine care turned every day into a joy. His daily surprises with local food, his stories, and his kind guidance made us experience India not as visitors but as family.

A special mention also goes to our wonderful driver, Shubhram, whose calmness, skill, and friendly presence made long journeys smooth and safe.

If you are planning to visit India — especially for your first time — we cannot recommend Wanderlust Travel Hub highly enough. Raj creates journeys that are not just well-organized and safe, but deeply personal. Every lodge, guide, and experience feels handpicked with love and authenticity.

We will carry India — and Raj — in our hearts forever.

Both are in the Eastern Himalayas. Both are spectacular. But they give you very different experiences.

Best beaches in Kerala - Varkala, Kovalam & Alleppey
Kerala has 600 km of coastline. These are the 3 beaches actually worth your time.

Varkala - the cliff beach
Red laterite cliffs towering over the Arabian Sea. This is the one that doesn't look real in photos. The northern end is safest for swimming. Surf schools available. Best for: couples, backpackers, those who want something dramatic.

Kovalam - the most complete beach destination
Three connected bays: Lighthouse Beach (most popular), Hawa Beach (calmer), and Samudra Beach. Parasailing, catamaran rides, ayurvedic spas, and a solid lineup of restaurants. Best for: first-timers, families, those who want everything in one place.

Alleppey - not a beach but a must
Technically a backwater destination, but the combination of beach + houseboat + lagoon makes it essential on any Kerala trip. Best for: houseboat experience, couples, anyone who wants to slow down.

When to go:
→ October to March: ideal — dry, calm sea, swimming-safe
→ June to September: no swimming, but the landscape is extraordinary and Ayurveda treatments are considered best this season
→ April–May: hot but good for domestic travellers

featured_reviews.name: Poulomi Saha
featured_reviews.review_text:
Bhakti and the Eastern Travels team transformed our special celebration into a front-row seat to nature’s greatest reality show! Like nature’s bingo, we checked off the “Big 5” and also spotted the delightfully named “Ugly 5.” The game drives were spectacular – we witnessed incredible wildlife in their natural habitat. We saw lions in double digits lounging like royalty, elephants commandeering the savanna highways, giraffes gracefully ambling across the landscape, and yes, we even saw a real “zebra crossing”!

Our guide John was knowledgeable and passionate, sharing fascinating insights about the ecosystem and local culture. He was an absolute superstar with an uncanny ability to spot a leopard at 200 meters. We encountered not one but two elusive leopards, proving that even the most camera-shy cats can’t resist a good photoshoot when the lighting is right!

We really appreciate how Bhakti and her team went the extra mile to make our special family occasion even more memorable. Her team outdid themselves by meticulously planning and executing the celebration with energy and care. Kudos to Bhakti and the whole Eastern Travels team!

Between witnessing the Great Migration’s drama, learning traditional fire-starting (harder than YouTube makes it look), and understanding why cattle equal currency, we gained new perspectives on how to elevate the art of living authentically.

Here’s a painting I created, inspired by life in the savanna!

The locations of the chosen hotels were extremely convenient from the perspective of proximity to the Rail stations, restaurants and general conveniences, and the rooms very comfortable, a couple of them had great views
The itinerary and sightseeing schedules ensured that we weren’t rushed at all and allowed for plenty of flexibility.
It was a wonderful change to be parked in the fabulously pretty quiet country small town Grindelwald for 4 nights as against the bustling crowded Interlaken, with equally easy access to various locales.
We thoroughly enjoyed visiting various small towns/quasi villages like, Brienz, Lavaux, Lauterbrunnen (lovely easy walks through flower filled meadows with the back drop of numerous waterfalls) , Gruyere ( much more to it than the cheese factory) Broc ( Cailler chocolate factory and more ) ; apart from the very well known tourist hotspots .
The quality of the food (though expensive) was outstanding, the ingredients, especially the cheeses ( as in the Fondue and Raclette), herbs   and the vegetables top class
Big shout of thanks for team Eastern especially Ms Nupur, Ms Tamasha and Mr Soumya for putting it all together.

We travelled on a Northern Lights tour with VOYAAH in November 2025.
Initially, the group size was around 15 people; however, due to sudden cancellations, the group reduced to only 6 participants.
We are fully aware that the package price offered was calculated based on a larger group size and was extremely competitive compared to the market. Operating the tour with only six guests would have been economically unviable for most operators. However, honoring the commitment made by Sharmishtha Ma’am, VOYAAH ensured that the tour operated smoothly and without compromise—and it turned out to be a wonderful experience.
Everything promised in the itinerary was 100% delivered. In fact, because of the smaller group size, we were able to visit several additional places that were not originally part of the itinerary, which added great value to the experience.
Although there was no dedicated tour manager due to the small group size, the driver-cum-guide, Mr. Manveer, was extremely cooperative, courteous, and knowledgeable. He ensured our comfort throughout the journey and made the experience enjoyable.
The hotels provided were all 4-star properties such as Radisson Blu and Crowne Plaza, located in the city center. This allowed us to experience the local vibe and nightlife comfortably.
There were some issues during the last two days due to miscommunication between vendors; however, these were later resolved satisfactorily by the VOYAAH team.
Daily lunch or dinner arrangements were made at Indian restaurants, as per our preference, which was greatly appreciated. The vehicle provided for the tour was also in very good condition.
From the beginning, Mr. Mayank Singh, Marketing Executive (Mumbai), ensured seamless coordination for visa processing, tour-related information, and other arrangements, which made the pre-tour experience smooth and stress-free.
One area where VOYAAH can improve is communication during the tour. Having a dedicated single point of contact throughout the journey would help in addressing both minor and major concerns more efficiently, as the driver-cum-guide did not have decision-making authority and had to depend on instructions from the Bangalore/Mumbai office.
Overall, it was a very memorable and enjoyable experience. Despite operational challenges, VOYAAH stood by their commitment and delivered an excellent tour.
I would definitely recommend VOYAAH for international tours and look forward to engaging with them again for our future travels.
Thank you, VOYAAH team!
